intelligence.essence: RLQ Implementation Refinement Law: a formal safety guarantee may be claimed for NayaNET only when every concrete authority-changing operation is mapped to a verified abstract transition, every required atomicity and ordering assumption is independently justified, and adversarial real execution histories are consistent with the reference model. Model correctness ≠ implementation correctness. The acceptance hierarchy: abstract model proved → implementation mapping established → real transactional and gateway semantics independently validated → production-scope qualification. No earlier rung automatically proves a later one. The hardest boundary is the external action gateway: without a participating fence, the honest claim is 'no new external request is authorized after revocation,' never 'no external effect can occur after revocation.' Every refinement certificate must state its exclusions.
intelligence.falsifier: A concrete stale commit the model forbids (refinement fails regardless of model-checker PASS); an authority-changing operation hidden as an 'administrative' stuttering step; SERIALIZABLE claimed as a design proof without conflict-detection/retry semantics; an unqualified claim of post-revocation external-effect safety without a participating fence; a green integration test presented as discharging the atomic-transition obligation; a worker's 'applied event' report accepted as VERIFY; a replica used as sole authority for current certification.

human_view.meaning: Proving the blueprint is safe is only half the job — now prove the actual building follows the blueprint. Every real thing that can change authority — database transactions, the scheduler, recovery workers, the read-time checks, the action gateway — must be mapped onto the model, operation by operation, and every assumption the model makes (transactions are atomic, revocations and publications can't slip past each other, crashes don't lose committed work) must be independently justified against the real database and real failure modes. Six separate boundaries, each proven on its own, then shown to compose. The hardest one is the outside world: once we hand a request to an external service, no database transaction can reach out and stop it — so the certificate must honestly say which boundary it covers and never claim more. The first real proof is a single race: pause a publisher at the database boundary, commit a real revocation, resume it, and show the stale write gets rejected by the actual system.

intelligence.learning_lesson: This completes the verification triad: RLQ-1 proves the abstract model, RLQ-MUT-1 proves the checker, RLQ-Refinement proves the implementation. The permanent pattern for every future law: three proof layers, each unable to stand alone (model checking can't see the database; the refinement argument can't see the runtime; experiments can't see the universal). The external-gateway honesty rule is the durable contribution — every safety certificate states exactly which boundary it covers and names its exclusions. And the hierarchy is the mnemonic: no earlier rung proves a later one.
